disciplines.label: Control, Command & Signalling
disciplines.scope_note: Signalling and control systems. Often procured separately; out of scope by default.

disciplines.label: Earthworks
disciplines.scope_note: Bulk fill, cut, soil improvement, slope stabilisation. Kept separate from substructure because the material flows differ.

disciplines.label: Energy / Electrification
disciplines.scope_note: OCS, substations, SCADA. Often procured separately; out of scope by default.

disciplines.label: MEP
disciplines.scope_note: Building services. Out of scope by default; switching it on also means moving the `stations` rows that were really MEP.

disciplines.label: Stations
disciplines.scope_note: Terminals, platforms, depots, maintenance buildings, architectural - and their MEP until the mep discipline is switched on.

disciplines.label: Structures
disciplines.scope_note: Bridges, viaducts, retaining walls, noise barriers.

disciplines.label: Substructure
disciplines.scope_note: Formation beneath the running surface, drainage, culverts, cable channels, ducts and chambers. Drainage is civils here, not MEP.

disciplines.label: Superstructure
disciplines.scope_note: The running surface: ballast, sleepers, rails, fastenings, switches and crossings on a railway; pavement layers on a road.

disciplines.label: Temporary Works
disciplines.scope_note: Construction bases, hardstanding, access roads, site facilities.

disciplines.label: Utilities
disciplines.scope_note: Third-party diversions and protections - HV, telecom, water, gas. Standalone because lead times run years and it gates everything downstream.

_readme: Synthetic demo tenant — the Wolds Link, a fictional ~32 km rail corridor in the East Midlands. Nothing in it is anyone's data. Import into an EMPTY tenant (POST /api/admin/tenant/import), then bake the network (HERE) — routes read UNBAKED until then. Diesel index: type the DESNZ weekly price on Config (fuel_index below is applied on import if the GB row is empty).
